name: Harvest
verdict: Self-serve: create an OAuth2 application at id.getharvest.com/developers with an HTTPS redirect URL, in about 1-3 days. No review or partner program was found.
needGuide: Short one: create the OAuth2 app, register the redirect URL, ship.

auth.detail: Authorization code (server-side) and implicit grant via Harvest ID: authorize at id.getharvest.com/oauth2/authorize, exchange at /api/v2/oauth2/token. Docs example shows a 14-day access token (expires_in 1209600) and a refresh_token grant; refresh token lifetime not stated; PKCE not mentioned. Apps can support multiple Harvest/Forecast accounts per user.

approval.gate: None documented: no review or partner program found for OAuth2 apps; the redirect URL is registered and a custom redirect_uri must start with it.

scopes.why: Coarse scopes only: you choose products and accounts, not read or write.
scopes.summary: Coarse scopes only: all, harvest:{ACCOUNT_ID}, forecast:{ACCOUNT_ID}, harvest:all, forecast:all, so you choose products and accounts rather than read/write. Docs recommend minimal scope. No review is tied to scopes.

cost: Free to register; a Harvest account is needed to test
prerequisites: Account and owner: Any Harvest ID holder can create an OAuth2 app; use a company-owned Harvest ID.
Where you register: id.getharvest.com/developers → Create new OAuth2 Application → name, redirect URL, multiple-accounts option, products (Harvest, Forecast or both)
Cost: Free to register; a Harvest account is needed to test

registerAt.path: id.getharvest.com/developers → Create new OAuth2 Application → name, redirect URL, multiple-accounts option, products (Harvest, Forecast or both)

steps.do: Sign in at id.getharvest.com/developers with the company Harvest ID and click Create new OAuth2 Application
Enter name, HTTPS redirect URL, choose multiple accounts, and select Harvest and/or Forecast products; record client ID and secret
Implement the server-side authorization code flow with a state parameter and exchange at /api/v2/oauth2/token
Call id.getharvest.com/api/v2/accounts to list the user's accounts and store the Harvest-Account-Id per connection
Send every request with a User-Agent naming the app and a contact email, and a Harvest-Account-Id header
Implement refresh_token handling before the 14-day expiry and re-auth on failure
Test with a second Harvest account including multi-account users

roles.team: Any Harvest ID holder can create an OAuth2 app; use a company-owned Harvest ID.
roles.customer: The user authorizes and picks the Harvest/Forecast account(s). Access follows the user's role in each account (account admins see more). Admin controls over third-party apps not documented.

testing: Use your own Harvest ID and a personal access token for quick calls; run the OAuth flow with a second Harvest account.
A Harvest free trial account is likely usable for testing (not confirmed).
The id.getharvest.com page itself could not be fetched (robots.txt).

blockers.problem: User with several accounts needs account selection
blockers.fix: List accounts and store the account ID, or API calls fail.

blockers.problem: Implicit grant exposes tokens in the browser
blockers.fix: Use authorization code on a backend.
Handle refresh failures with a clear re-connect prompt.

blockers.problem: No granular scopes, so access equals the user's role
blockers.fix: Minimize what your agent calls and disclose it.

automation.agentCan: Write the OAuth and refresh code, account-selection logic, headers, and test API calls, and draft customer-facing connection text.
automation.humanMust: Harvest ID sign-in to register the app, store secrets, and customer-side authorization.

uncertain: Refresh token lifetime, rate limits, PKCE support, admin controls, and any listing process were not confirmed; the developers console and OAuth help pages could not be fetched.
